document_summary: Justia mirror of California Civil Code § 1946.2 (2025), the Tenant Protection Act's statewide just-cause eviction and relocation-assistance rule for residential tenancies in California.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause Eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without a stated just cause (at-fault or no-fault). For no-fault terminations the owner must pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months' occupancy; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent (paid within 15 calendar days of notice) or final-month rent waiver
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months, or 24 months if additional adult tenants were added to the lease before 24 months (then either all tenants have 12+ months or one has 24+ months).
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; certain nonprofit hospital, religious, care facilities; dormitories; shared bath/kitchen with owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property not owned by REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member (with required written notice); deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property covered by a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a later local ordinance that is more protective (with binding finding); a less protective post-9/1/2019 local ordinance is not enforced. Property cannot be subject to both.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date taken from subdivision (m): 'This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.' Section as amended by AB 1529 (Stats. 2025, ch. 203), effective January 1, 2026; repealed as of January 1, 2030 by its own terms. Text also references earlier July 1, 2020 notice dates, which are application dates and not used. Secondary source (Justia mirror); official code is the underlying law.
